Hospital infection control staff members identified 42 cases from among the 136 residents (attack rate = 31%).
C. perfringens enterotoxin (CPE) was detected in 20 of 23 stool specimens from ill residents and staff members.
The most common symptoms were diarrhea (94%), abdominal cramps (51%), nausea (39%), and vomiting (27%).

CDC joined the investigation on May 13 to help identify the outbreak cause.
